Documentation → Releases → All releases

Releases

Every SATOM version in plain language — what was new, what changed for you, what was fixed and what to check before upgrading.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
On this page
  • SATOM 3.x
  • SATOM 2.x
  • SATOM 1.x
  • SATOM 0.x

Each SATOM version has its own page here: what is new, what works differently, what was fixed and — when it matters — what to check before you upgrade. They are written for the people who run SATOM, not for its developers.

💡Tip — Which version am I running?

The version is shown in the console footer and on Software Update. Upgrading is covered in Software update and, for isolated networks, Offline update packages.

SATOM 3.x#

Version Released In short
3.4.1 Oct 21, 2026 Documentation: the API SATOM exposes to your systems is named the SATOM API — its own manual title, Features section, navigation entry and Documentation Center category. No behaviour changes.
3.4.0 Oct 21, 2026 SATOM mapped to the NAF Framework: the API describes itself and reads and writes templates, bindings and baselines, configuration history, findings and metrics; intent deviation findings; processes started by events, schedules and the API with a Compensate step; SNMP polling and a syslog receiver; the Documentation Center on every node; CPU, memory and disk history of the nodes.
3.3.8 Oct 20, 2026 Python Studio: data stores, connections, apps shared with groups or people, FortiGate and NetBox examples, and a security review that bounds what Studio code can do to SATOM; themes imported from a site.
3.3.7 Oct 19, 2026 An update from the repository installs its dependencies from the Update sources index; SQLAlchemy 2.1.5 and paramiko 5.1.0.
3.3.6 Oct 19, 2026 Update packages and Python libraries from another URL — an internal pipeline or mirror, public or with a user and token — and Libraries no longer reports packages it could not check as up to date.
3.3.5 Oct 19, 2026 A single click on a list row selects it, so Clone, Save as template and Delete work on it; a double-click opens it.
3.3.4 Oct 19, 2026 Names built from the host and the port with your own regex variables, segments with several networks tried in order, and the sandbox working on SLES / openSUSE Leap 15.
3.3.3 Oct 18, 2026 Deploy clones — copy one installation's configuration into another, from the shell or from Settings — and update packages that ship only the wheels a node can be missing.
3.3.2 Oct 17, 2026 An update from 2.x now finishes itself — the Script Library unit, the SQL console role and the 3.x scheduled actions — instead of ending green with the node half-done.
3.3.1 Oct 16, 2026 The FortiAnalyzer schema harvest runs one path everywhere — build read off the box, a failed walk kept with its reason — and the harvest command no longer answers "unsupported" for FortiAnalyzer or FortiAuthenticator.
3.3.0 Oct 16, 2026 Operations opens on a Wiki the team writes for itself, the HTTP Observatory reverts its own fixes and adds a Content Security Policy in Report-Only first, and device alerts say which reading crossed which limit.
3.2.1 Oct 16, 2026 Pick the sites the HTTP Observatory grades from a searchable checkbox list instead of a table of every policy, and two fixes to that page.
3.2.0 Oct 16, 2026 An HTTP Observatory grades every site your appliances publish and fixes it on the FortiWeb, the Transaction Tracer becomes a page with cookies and a HAR viewer, profiles can be confined to some ADOMs, and Studio gains a Script Library with database-fed forms.
3.1.0 Oct 13, 2026 All five products are now drawn from their own measured GUI, every field only the CLI has is shown and editable, every write is checked on the device, and Naming Discovery finds the convention your devices already follow.
3.0.0 Oct 8, 2026 SATOM stops reading Fortinet's website itself and gets its vendor knowledge from signed knowledge packs, warns when a FortiWeb's signature database goes stale, and adds a read-only FortiGate workspace.

SATOM 2.x#

Version Released In short
2.13.0 Oct 7, 2026 SATOM learns what each firmware build really supports, over both the REST API and the CLI, and uses it to check every write, predict whether a configuration survives an upgrade, and write fields only the CLI can set.
2.12.0 Oct 6, 2026 Templates now know which firmware build they were written for and are checked against every target build, predefined protection profiles are cached in a factory catalog, and deep rediscovery is much faster.
2.11.0 Oct 3, 2026 A large security and consistency release — every page and action now enforces its own permission, passwords and idle sessions follow one policy, privileged actions are audited, and a long list of everyday problems is fixed.
2.10.1 Oct 3, 2026 Stop now really stops a rediscovery during its deep capture, and keeps your previous deep capture intact.
2.10.0 Oct 3, 2026 Job notices can be minimised, the deep capture shows real progress, and Device health is filled in right after a rediscovery.
2.9.1 Oct 2, 2026 A discovery with wrong credentials no longer locks the FortiWeb admin account or wipes the last good snapshot.
2.9.0 Oct 2, 2026 Every action you take on a device now runs as a background job that shows its progress, and writes to the same device queue instead of colliding.
2.8.0 Oct 2, 2026 Rediscovery finally uses your imported CAs, rediscovery gets a Stop button, and Node TLS certificate changes show each step and warn about the web server reload.
2.7.0 Oct 2, 2026 A node can now fetch its own signed update package online, updates bring the new API pack with them, and Node TLS can generate certificate requests.
2.6.0 Oct 2, 2026 API packs carry SATOM's knowledge of vendor APIs to offline nodes, and a running update now shows the step it is on.
2.5.0 Oct 1, 2026 Every release now ships a signed offline update package, offline-installed nodes can finally apply it, and the console no longer reaches out to the Internet.
2.4.1 Sep 29, 2026 Docker installs from the published source work again, and every release now publishes a ready-made container image.
2.4.0 Sep 28, 2026 The API endpoint list is now pinned to a specific firmware build and refreshed from measurements, and this release also delivers everything prepared for 2.3.0.
2.3.0 Sep 26, 2026 Never published on its own — its Docker operations agent and Docker fixes reached users in 2.4.0.
2.2.0 Sep 26, 2026 SATOM now keeps a versioned API library for every product, and firmware answers, pre-flights and the API explorer are based on it.
2.1.3 Sep 24, 2026 The installers now speak English, the published manual has no broken links, and a dedicated Docker Compose manual is available.
2.1.2 Sep 24, 2026 Fresh installations work again, the container image creates its first admin, ufw is opened, and a new guided installer sets up a machine in one go.
2.1.1 Sep 23, 2026 New installations no longer start with a published default admin password, and splitting a change into waves keeps your choices.
2.1.0 Sep 22, 2026 Scout now reads Fortinet's upgrade notes and warns you before a firmware push, open change requests can be edited, devices can be put into maintenance with one click, and the API catalog learns what each exact firmware build serves over REST and the CLI.
2.0.0 Sep 10, 2026 A major release that adds Scout, the Fleet Calendar, Process, the Device Console, fleet-wide WAF views and a guided New Server Policy build, and removes two artifact controls.

SATOM 1.x#

Version Released In short
1.20.0 Aug 24, 2026 Sentinel's four working pages now carry "?" explanations beside their controls, including the health indicators on the incidents console.
1.19.0 Aug 23, 2026 Sentinel can now publish a border blocklist that your FortiGates read as a threat feed, with time-limited entries, a recorded release action and an optional audit copy in git.
1.18.0 Aug 23, 2026 Sentinel can now ask the firewall in front of an appliance, through FortiAnalyzer, whether an attacking address is a real peer, and uses the answer as evidence and as a safety veto.
1.17.1 Aug 23, 2026 Two Sentinel buttons that should switch to a neighbouring pane did nothing; they now work.
1.17.0 Aug 23, 2026 All of Sentinel's surfaces now live in the Admin Console, Sentinel gains four named operating modes, and an on-demand sweep runs as a job over the devices you choose.
1.16.1 Aug 23, 2026 The Admin Console side menu opens again, and ten other page features that the browser had been silently blocking now work.
1.16.0 Aug 23, 2026 Every control on the Sentinel settings page now has a "?" that explains, on hover, what it does and what happens at each extreme.
1.15.0 Aug 23, 2026 Sentinel's Architecture and Incidents console now open inside the Admin Console, next to its settings, instead of taking you to another page.
1.14.0 Aug 23, 2026 The Admin Console menu is now the same everywhere, the stand-alone Sentinel settings page keeps it, and Sentinel moves to the bottom of the menu.
1.13.0 Aug 23, 2026 Settings → Sentinel becomes a full section that shows what Sentinel does before it shows a single setting, with a demo lab you can run safely.
1.12.0 Aug 22, 2026 Policy cloning now copies SNI policies, certificates and profile settings it used to miss, and a declined section is finally left exactly as the destination had it.
1.11.0 Aug 20, 2026 Introduces Sentinel for security incident correlation and controlled response, external vault storage for credentials, the WAF Artifacts store, and ADOM-aware handling of physical appliances.
1.10.1 Aug 17, 2026 A repair release that makes three buttons work again and gives the three new diagnostic tools the same look as the rest of the Tools menu.
1.10.0 Aug 17, 2026 Adds Upgrade Flow for whole maintenance windows, three diagnostic tools, the bookmarks rail and Concept Map, alert routing with syslog and webhook delivery, issue-tracker tickets, and an external API for WAF exceptions.
1.9.3 Aug 10, 2026 SATOM speaks your language, change requests become a complete, signable change process for every Forti product, and directory sign-in gains RADIUS import, an approval gate and several sources in order.
1.9.2 Aug 9, 2026 The object editor now offers a dropdown wherever a field must name an existing object, and checks those names on the appliance before saving.
1.9.1 Aug 9, 2026 Cloning and migrating FortiWeb configuration now copies everything an object needs, the clone shows what it will and will not copy, and every audit entry shows its ID.
1.9.0 Aug 8, 2026 The Attack ID page becomes a full investigation and exception workbench — field-by-field explanations, AI questions per field, exceptions built from the fields you tick and inserted from the same page.
1.8.0 Aug 7, 2026 The AI Advisor streams its answers, can be stopped, uses read-only tools and reports time and cost per reply, and Settings → General gains a Services card to start, stop and restart services on both nodes.
1.7.1 Aug 7, 2026 Fixes the sealed recovery envelope introduced in 1.7.0, which could not reach the standby or any backup, and documents recovery custody in the operator manual.
1.7.0 Aug 7, 2026 Introduces the AI Advisor for false-positive triage and Lua drafting, and adds sealed recovery custody so a rebuilt node can read its restored secrets.
1.6.0 Aug 7, 2026 Metrics collection reaches FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator and FortiAnalyzer, dashboards gain device pickers, and the published manual and release notes become searchable.
1.5.0 Aug 6, 2026 Thresholds you set once per product, building appliances from nothing on Proxmox VE or VMware ESXi, a trust store for your own CAs, and FortiAuthenticator as a fully managed product.
1.4.1 Aug 5, 2026 SATOM health now reports the installation's own HA state, and appliance HA counts moved to Device health where they belong.
1.4.0 Aug 5, 2026 A fleet metrics store with Analytics boards and period reports, signed offline update packages, separate SATOM and Device health pages, and a move to the Elastic License 2.0.
1.3.5 Aug 4, 2026 Signing in now works behind a NAT or proxy on a non-standard port, and the node certificate covers the DNS names you actually use.
1.3.4 Aug 4, 2026 The offline install bundles now include git, without which one of the backup copies was never made on air-gapped nodes.
1.3.3 Aug 4, 2026 The installer no longer stops the web server it has just started on openSUSE, and two false warnings on standalone nodes are gone.
1.3.2 Aug 4, 2026 The installer now completes on openSUSE and RHEL, fails loudly when something goes wrong, and reminds you to switch on the scheduled protections.
1.3.1 Aug 3, 2026 Rebuilt offline bundles, factory settings that no longer point at someone else's network, a new manual for the device APIs, and the documentation published in one place only.
1.3 Aug 2, 2026 An operator console for when the web interface is down, a Service Monitor with per-policy traffic, two years of monitoring history, honest health badges and alerts, and an installer that works on openSUSE.
1.2.2 Jul 27, 2026 Certificate renewal, Node TLS and the Certificate Manager work again after a fault shipped in the 1.2 and 1.2.1 bundles.
1.2.1 Jul 27, 2026 A documentation release that adds the safeguards catalog and spells out the protections you must switch on after a fresh install.
1.2 Jul 27, 2026 SATOM stops running as root, issues Let's Encrypt certificates through your DNS provider, keeps its code repository safe through git outages, and takes the name SATOM.
1.1 Jul 15, 2026 The services, folders and installers take the SATOM name; existing installations migrate with a script.
1.0 Jul 14, 2026 The first production release, with DNS record management, an alert engine, certificate auto-renewal, configuration drift detection, safer restores and a Linux installer.

SATOM 0.x#

Version Released In short
0.9 Jul 13, 2026 Encrypted traffic between SATOM nodes, with an internal certificate authority and live "encryption in transit" monitoring.
0.8 Jul 12, 2026 FortiAnalyzer becomes a full ADOM, FortiADC configurations join the source of truth, and backups gain a coverage page and an external backup server.

SATOM 3.4.1A documentation release — the API SATOM exposes to your systems is named and presented as the SATOM API, with its own manual title, its own section on the Features page, its own place in the site navigation and its own category in the Documentation Center, so it can no longer be confused with the Fortinet device APIs SATOM drives internally.SATOM 3.4.0SATOM mapped to the NAF Framework — the API describes itself and reads and writes desired state, configuration history, findings and metrics; a device that no longer matches its template is a finding; processes start from events, schedules and the API and can undo their own writes; SNMP polling and a syslog receiver; the Documentation Center on every node; CPU, memory and disk history of the nodes; the rest of the Wiki.SATOM 3.3.8Python Studio — Script Library and console on one page, data stores, connections to external APIs and databases, apps with a form, a diagram and actions shared with groups or people, working FortiGate and NetBox examples, and a security review that bounds what Studio code can do to SATOM; plus themes imported from a website or another SATOM node.Software UpdateUpdate SATOM's own code and Python dependencies — from the git remote or from a signed offline package — through a privileged runner, standby first on a pair.Offline update packagesUpdate a node with no route to the code repository — a signed package with the application and the Python wheels it may be missing, verified against a root-owned trust store and applied by the privileged runner with automatic rollback.
